data.narrative:
DiamFab is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Khaled Driche, Gauthier Chicot, and Ivan Llaurado, having raised €8.7M to date. The broader Chips & Semiconductors sector comprises 11 private peers and 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD), with notable private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The seed-stage cohort within semiconductors contains insufficient narrow-filter comparables—zero same-stage peers, one adjacent-stage peer, and zero similar-tier valuations—falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for statistical reliability. An all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise, given the heterogeneity of semiconductor subsegments and the company's frontier positioning.

The analysis reveals a structural constraint common to early-stage deep-tech: comparable transactions at equivalent stages and competitive scope are sparse. While the sector peer universe is reasonably populated at later stages (the five named private peers represent growth/later rounds), seed-stage semiconductor valuations lack sufficient transaction density for triangulation. This gap suggests that DiamFab's valuation will likely depend more heavily on investor-specific due diligence—technical feasibility, IP defensibility, and founder track record—than on market multiples. Any valuation range at this stage should be treated as highly provisional pending either additional seed-round datapoints or disclosure of the company's specific technical differentiation and addressable market.
